CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ankle pain and swelling

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
36-year-old female presents with left ankle pain and swelling that occurred two days ago after slipping on ice and snow while walking to her car. Patient fell and her left ankle twisted, particularly on the outside of the ankle. After the fall, she experienced significant swelling and pain that makes ambulation difficult. She has tried ibuprofen, ice, and elevation with minimal relief. Pain is localized to the outside of the ankle with no pain in the calf, lower leg, or knee. No bleeding reported.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies pain above the ankle, calf pain, lower leg pain, or knee pain. No bleeding noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Diabetes mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin for diabetes
Norvasc for hypertension

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neck exam: No bruits. Lungs: Clear. Heart: Normal with 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, unchanged from prior. Abdomen: Good. Left ankle: Tenderness over lateral malleolus and fifth metatarsal. Swelling and redness present. Pain with valgus stressing of ankle. Normal sensation and normal pulses distally.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Ankle sprain with rule out fracture. X-ray of left ankle ordered due to tenderness over fifth metatarsal. Patient placed in air splint with crutches and instructed to avoid weight-bearing pending x-ray results. Naproxen 500 mg twice daily for pain control. Continue ice and elevation. If x-ray reveals fracture, patient will be referred to orthopedics. If no fracture, will progress to partial weight-bearing. Diabetes: Continue metformin. Hemoglobin A1c and baseline labs ordered. Patient to keep ophthalmology appointment already scheduled. Hypertension: Norvasc refilled. Continue monitoring blood pressure.
